So if you had on that 100 mile flight, you had 100 seats and only 75 passengers in those seats, then your revenue passenger miles would be 7500, 75 times 100.

So if you saw that an airline was increasing ASM year over year by 10%, then you could conclude that their capacity is increasing by 10%.

And the best metric that incorporates all of this and the most important term when talking about the revenue side of an airline is RASM.

So if the airline is increasing RASM year over year, then that means on a per unit basis, they're generating more revenue than they were before.

Similarly, if the yield is going up, if they're getting more per customer, but they're flying fewer customers, RASM would go down.
So RASM is the most important relevant metric in revenue management. We always maximize RASM.
We never maximize load or yield because that could actually be suboptimal to the airline's network.

So the airline takes its total cost, spreads them across all of the seat miles that they have, and come up with one number that they can then compare to RASM.
